type: PINNED wrk2 CO-free latency-load curve — the pinned re-run of the superseded 20260722-203502
pinning: VERIFIED live: targets 0-1,8-9 / loadgen 2-3,10-11 / DB 4-7,12-15 (tuned-PG). claim-status pinned_cpus=4. This is the fix vs 20260722-203502 (pinned_cpus=0, unpinned cpuset 0-15).
driver: wrk2 open-loop fixed offered rate (percentiles = service time). Sequential single-target within each pair (run_wrk_target FIRST then SECOND, co-locator resident but not driven).
shape: 3 pairs x ab/ba x (5 heavy + 5 light) = 60 leaves. 120s window. n=4 per (target,rung) via pair/order redundancy in lean-co-resident pairs.
ladders: heavy 2000/4000/6000/8000/10000 (below ~11k DB ceiling); light 6000/12000/18000/24000/30000 (sub-saturation: probed pinned light saturation qhib=44275, qtuned~48k, exeris~57k; top 30k=68% of qhib).

clean_light_p99_ms.note: per target from its LEAN-co-resident pair (exeris & qtuned from pair-1, qhib from pair-2), mean ab+ba, publishable-only.

light_finding: CLEAN curves: exeris FLAT ~1.5-2.2ms across 6-30k (best tail), qtuned rises to 5.2ms@30k, qhib rises fastest to 7.3ms@30k. Ordering exeris<qtuned<qhib at every rung. In the clean (lean-co-resident) pairs, pinned ~= unpinned (~1.5-2.5ms overlap) — light single-read is cheap, so pinning did not change clean light latency; the pinned run extends to 30k and reveals the tail climb.
heavy_finding: Pinning genuinely helped HEAVY: exeris/qtuned p99 improved -0.2 to -1.9ms (jitter removal); the unpinned qtuned 6k p99=138ms contention spike -> 3.12ms pinned. At 10k (near DB ceiling): exeris 16ms=GC-tail (0.25x heap), qhib 19ms=CPU-starvation (pinned 4 cores insufficient for the CPU-hungry ORM), qtuned 4.5ms best. Both campaigns 0 non-publishable heavy leaves.
KEY_FINDING_pair3_coresidence: The catastrophic 20-37s light degeneracy is PAIR 3 (qhib+qtuned, two heavy JVMs co-resident) and PINNING DID NOT FIX IT: pinned pair-3 qtuned p99 = 2430/8490ms@12k, 27510/22580ms@18k (vs unpinned 22020/32440ms). It is NOT an unpinning artifact — it is CO-RESIDENCE: the idle-but-resident heavy qhib JVM steals cycles from the driven qtuned on the shared slice. Non-monotonic (clean 6k -> broken 12-18k -> clean 24-30k) => transient (qhib JIT/GC warmup). Pair-1 (lean exeris co-resident) is pristine. This is the two-heavy-targets topology risk. A clean pair-3 comparison needs TRULY single-target (co-resident NOT launched); the pairwise harness cannot give it.
non_publishable_leaves: 3 (all pair-3 qtuned, correctly flagged by the attain<99% gate): light/12000 ba (qtuned attain 93%), light/18000 ab (79%), light/18000 ba (81%). The 12000 ab pair-3 leaf passed the attain gate (>=99%) but still had p99 2430ms — attain alone does not catch every co-residence tail spike.
supersedes_relation: This is the pinned re-run of 20260722-203502 (SUPERSEDED, unpinned). Correction chain: my earlier curve-notes wrongly blamed a wrk2 parser bug + missing attain gate (both false — harness was correct, commit 11937a2), then attributed the collapse to unpinning (this re-run shows it is co-residence, not pinning). Net: the harness parser/gate were always correct; the light collapse is a co-residence topology effect that pinning does not resolve.
caveats: Comparison-eligible per-target curve = lean-co-resident pairs (exeris & qtuned from pair-1, qhib from pair-2). Pair-3 (qhib-vs-qtuned) is co-residence-contaminated at 12-18k and must be excluded or re-measured single-target.
Heap asymmetry retained (exeris 0.25x / quarkus 0.75x of the triad budget) — exeris's near-ceiling tails (heavy 10k=16ms) are partly GC-pause, not pure service time.
